name: BITTLER RES (MICK & NANETTE)
address: 1654 NW WILD RYE CIRCLE, BEND, OR 97703

fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain clear passage for emergency vehicles.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, or stored materials that could block emergency vehicle entry.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the main residence and detached structure to reduce obstacles for responders working around the buildings.
• Mark any gate or gap in the perimeter fencing that allows rear access so responders can locate it without searching.
• Keep any rear access gate unlocked or secured with a breakaway lock to allow responders to reach the back of the property on foot.
• Thin dense vegetation between the detached structure and the main residence so responders can move between the two buildings without obstruction.
• Post a property map or address placard at the front entry that shows the location of the detached structure and any secondary access points.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the structure on all sides.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or within a few feet of the foundation and exterior walls.
• Clear dead leaves, branches, and plant debris from the roof and gutters regularly.
• Thin scattered shrubs around the structure so individual plants are not connected to each other or to nearby trees.
• Keep low branches on scattered trees trimmed up from the ground to reduce the path fire can travel from ground vegetation into the tree canopy.
• Clear overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs along the full length of the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway surface and edges free of dead plant material, especially during dry seasons.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency vehicles approaching from the road.
• Widen any narrow sections of the driveway where possible to allow large emergency vehicles to pass or turn around.
• Maintain the open clearing near the structure by keeping it free of shrub regrowth and accumulated dead plant material.
• Create a clear path around the rear of the structure by cutting back vegetation that limits movement close to the building.
• Remove or thin mixed vegetation patches that connect ground
